quote: Draft the ICH E3 §16 patient safety narrative from the collected case facts
error: ICH E3 does not put patient safety narratives in section 16. Section 16 holds the appendices, for example 16.2.7 adverse event listings and 16.3 CRFs. E3 places narratives of deaths, other serious AEs and certain other significant AEs in section 12.3.2 or section 14.3.3.
correct: Patient safety narratives per ICH E3 §12.3.2, placed in §12.3.2 or §14.3.3.
correctedText: Draft the ICH E3 §12.3.2 patient safety narrative (placed in the report text or §14.3.3) from the collected case facts

quote: Per 42 USC 262(c) and 21 CFR 600.21, FDA must inspect and approve the manufacturing facility before a BLA can be licensed.
error: 42 USC 262(c) is FDA's general authority to inspect biologics establishments, and 21 CFR 600.21 covers when inspections take place. Neither one sets the rule that a license issues only after inspection. That rule is in 21 CFR 601.20(d). The same pairing is cited again at line 816, and line 817 gives '21 CFR 600.21' as the reference.
correct: The pre-license inspection requirement is 21 CFR 601.20(d): a biologics license is issued only after inspection of the establishment(s) listed in the application. 21 CFR 600.21 covers inspection timing, and 42 USC 262(c) gives the inspection authority.
correctedText: Per 21 CFR 601.20(d), a biologics license is issued only after FDA inspects the establishment(s) listed in the BLA (inspection authority: 42 USC 262(c); timing: 21 CFR 600.21).

quote: Per 21 CFR 610.2, samples and protocols must be submitted to CBER for lot release before distribution of vaccines and blood products.
error: 21 CFR 610.2(a) does not impose automatic lot release on every vaccine and blood product. CBER can require samples and protocols for any lot at any time, and a lot may not be distributed before release only after the manufacturer is notified by the Director, CBER. Whole blood and blood components are also generally not subject to CBER lot release. Plasma derivatives can be, when CBER so notifies the manufacturer.
correct: Under 21 CFR 610.2(a), CBER may require samples of any lot, with protocols, at any time. Once the manufacturer has been notified by the Director, CBER, it may not distribute a lot until CBER releases it. Most vaccines and plasma-derived products are under routine lot release by such notification. It is not a blanket requirement for all blood products.
correctedText: Per 21 CFR 610.2(a), CBER may require samples of any lot, with protocols showing test results, at any time; once notified by the Director, CBER, the manufacturer may not distribute a lot until CBER releases it. Most vaccines and many plasma-derived products are under routine lot release on this basis; it is not a blanket requirement for all blood products.

quote: Per ICH S6(R1) and ICH S8, immunotoxicity assessment is especially important for immunomodulatory biologics.
error: ICH S8 (Immunotoxicity Studies for Human Pharmaceuticals) excludes biotechnology-derived products from its scope. Its scope section says it does not apply to products covered by ICH S6. Citing S8 as authority for immunotoxicity assessment of biologics is a misapplied citation.
correct: For biologics, immunotoxicity assessment is covered by ICH S6(R1) (Part I section 4.5, and the immunomodulation considerations in the Addendum). ICH S8 applies to small-molecule pharmaceuticals and explicitly excludes biotechnology-derived products.
correctedText: Per ICH S6(R1), immunotoxicity assessment is especially important for immunomodulatory biologics (ICH S8 does not apply to biotechnology-derived products).

quote: { value: 'pader', label: 'PADER (Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report)' },
error: For a licensed biologic, the US periodic safety report required by 21 CFR 600.80(c)(2) is the Periodic Adverse Experience Report (PAER). The PADER is the NDA/ANDA report under 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2). The options also leave out the PBRER, which FDA accepts in place of the PAER under a waiver, as line 1845 of this file says.
correct: For a BLA, the periodic report is the PAER under 21 CFR 600.80(c)(2), or an ICH E2C(R2) PBRER submitted under an FDA waiver. PADER is the drug (21 CFR 314.80) term.
correctedText: { value: 'pader', label: 'PAER (Periodic Adverse Experience Report, 21 CFR 600.80(c)(2))' },

quote: Fewer lots may not provide sufficient statistical power for the tiered analytical similarity assessment.
error: This text points to the tiered (Tier 1/2/3) analytical similarity approach. FDA withdrew that approach in 2018, as this file's own guidance at line 2033 says. The current 2019 draft comparative analytical assessment guidance uses risk-ranked quantitative or qualitative evaluation (for example, equivalence testing or a quality range), not tiers.
correct: Fewer than about 10 reference product lots may not adequately characterize reference product variability for the risk-based comparative analytical assessment, whether quantitative (for example, equivalence testing or a quality range) or qualitative. This is the approach of FDA's 2019 draft guidance on comparative analytical assessment for therapeutic protein biosimilars.
correctedText: Fewer lots may not adequately characterize reference product variability for the risk-based comparative analytical assessment (quantitative evaluation such as equivalence testing or a quality range, or qualitative evaluation, as justified by each attribute's risk ranking) described in FDA's current draft guidance on comparative analytical assessment for therapeutic protein biosimilars.

quote: placeholder: 'e.g., Division of Oncology Products 1, CDER',
error: CDER has not had a 'Division of Oncology Products 1' since the 2019-2020 reorganization of the Office of New Drugs. Oncology review divisions now sit in the Office of Oncologic Diseases, under names such as 'Division of Oncology 1'. The example shows clients a division name that no longer exists.
correct: e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, CDER
correctedText: placeholder: 'e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, CDER',

quote: FDA typically publishes its own briefing document 1-2 business days before the meeting.
error: Under FDA's 2008 Advisory Committee guidance, FDA makes briefing materials public no later than 2 full business days before the meeting. Posting 1 business day before would fall short of that. This line also contradicts line 76 of the same flow ('at least two business days before the meeting').
correct: FDA posts its briefing document, and the sponsor's, publicly no later than 2 business days before the meeting. In practice this is usually exactly 2 business days.
correctedText: FDA typically publishes its own briefing document no later than 2 business days before the meeting.

quote: Per ICH E1, FDA expects at least 1,500 patients exposed for chronic-use drugs, with at least 300-600 exposed for 6 months and 100 for 12 months.
error: This misstates ICH E1. E1 is an ICH guideline, not a stand-alone FDA expectation. It applies only to long-term treatment of non-life-threatening conditions, and it gives approximate figures: 'about 1500' in total and 300-600 for 6 months, not 'at least'. The first-pass correction at line 490 of the same file already states this scope limit. This helpText still states the old, overbroad version, so the two strings shown to the client contradict each other.
correct: Per ICH E1, for drugs intended for long-term (beyond 6 months) treatment of non-life-threatening conditions, the safety database is generally about 1,500 patients in total, 300-600 exposed for 6 months and at least 100 for 1 year; it does not apply to life-threatening indications.
correctedText: Per ICH E1, for drugs intended for long-term treatment (beyond 6 months) of non-life-threatening conditions, the safety database is generally about 1,500 patients exposed in total, 300-600 exposed for 6 months and at least 100 exposed for 1 year; these figures do not apply to life-threatening indications.

quote: Per EU MDR Article 61(11), CERs for implantable and Class III devices must be updated at least annually.
error: Article 61(11) requires the clinical evaluation to be updated throughout the device life cycle. For Class III and implantable devices, what it requires at least annually is the PMCF evaluation report and, if indicated, the SSCP, not the CER. The same misattribution appears in the option label at line 149.
correct: Article 61(11): clinical evaluation updated throughout the life cycle. For Class III and implantable devices, the PMCF evaluation report and, if indicated, the SSCP (Article 32) are updated at least annually.
correctedText: Per EU MDR Article 61(11), the clinical evaluation must be updated throughout the device life cycle with PMCF data; for implantable and Class III devices, the PMCF evaluation report and, if indicated, the SSCP (Article 32) must be updated at least annually, and the CER should be updated to reflect them.

quote: Annual (required for Class III and implantable per Article 61(11))
error: Article 61(11) makes the annual update apply to the PMCF evaluation report and the SSCP, not the CER itself.
correct: Annual update of the PMCF evaluation report and SSCP is required for Class III and implantable devices (Article 61(11)). The CER is updated throughout the life cycle with that data.
correctedText: Annual (aligned with the at-least-annual PMCF evaluation report and SSCP update required for Class III and implantable devices by Article 61(11))

quote: The CER must be reviewed and approved by the Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) per EU MDR Article 15
error: Article 15 does not require the PRRC to review or approve the CER. Article 15(3) makes the PRRC responsible for checking device conformity before release, keeping the technical documentation and EU declaration of conformity up to date, PMS obligations, vigilance reporting, and the clinical investigation statement.
correct: MDR Article 15(3) lists the PRRC's responsibilities, and CER approval is not among them. The CER is signed by the qualified clinical evaluators (MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 6.4).
correctedText: The CER must be signed and dated by suitably qualified clinical evaluators whose qualifications are documented (EU MDR Article 61 and Annex XIV; MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4). Approving the CER is not one of the PRRC's responsibilities under EU MDR Article 15

quote: MDCG 2020-7 provides detailed guidance on PMCF plan and PMCF evaluation report content.
error: MDCG 2020-7 is the PMCF Plan template only. The PMCF Evaluation Report template is MDCG 2020-8, which the file itself cites at line 261.
correct: MDCG 2020-7: PMCF Plan template. MDCG 2020-8: PMCF Evaluation Report template.
correctedText: MDCG 2020-7 provides a template and guidance for PMCF plan content; MDCG 2020-8 provides the corresponding template for the PMCF evaluation report.

quote: For Class III and implantable devices, a PMCF plan is always required.
error: The MDR does not exempt any class from the justification route. Annex III 1.1(b) and Annex XIV Part B allow, for any class, a PMCF plan or a justification of why PMCF is not applicable. A PMCF plan for Class III or implantable devices is an expectation, not an absolute legal rule.
correct: For all classes, including Class III and implantable devices, the MDR requires a PMCF plan or a justification of why PMCF is not applicable (Annex III 1.1(b)). For Class III and implantable devices that justification is rarely accepted.
correctedText: For Class III and implantable devices, a justification for not performing PMCF is rarely accepted, and Article 61(11) requires the PMCF evaluation report to be updated at least annually.

quote: Required for interventional PMCF studies per EU MDR Article 70
error: Article 70 governs applications for pre-market clinical investigations. Under Article 74(1), a PMCF investigation that adds invasive or burdensome procedures needs a notification to the Member States at least 30 days before it starts. That route does not go through the Article 70 application procedure.
correct: EU MDR Article 74(1): notify the Member States concerned at least 30 days before starting.
correctedText: Required for PMCF investigations involving additional invasive or burdensome procedures: notify the Member States concerned at least 30 days before start per EU MDR Article 74(1); if the device is used outside its intended purpose, the full clinical investigation application regime applies per Article 74(2)

quote: MDCG 2020-5 provides guidance on clinical evaluation adequacy and the clinical data sets that should be considered.
error: MDCG 2020-5 is 'Clinical Evaluation – Equivalence: A guide for manufacturers and notified bodies'. It covers demonstrating equivalence, not clinical evaluation adequacy or which clinical data sets to consider.
correct: MDCG 2020-5 covers equivalence. Sufficiency of clinical evidence is covered by MDCG 2020-6, and data identification by MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8.
correctedText: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8 provides guidance on identifying pertinent clinical data; where data from an equivalent device is used, MDCG 2020-5 provides guidance on demonstrating equivalence.

quote: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7, all data from the manufacturer's post-market surveillance system should be included.
error: Section 7 of MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 covers the scope of the clinical evaluation (Stage 0). Identifying pertinent data, including data generated and held by the manufacturer such as PMS data, is Section 8 (Stage 1, Section 8.1).
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8.1.
correctedText: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8.1 (data generated and held by the manufacturer), all data from the manufacturer's post-market surveillance system should be included.

quote: Under EU MDR Article 61(5), manufacturers demonstrating equivalence to a device of another manufacturer must have a contract in place
error: The Article 61(5) contract requirement applies only to implantable and Class III devices. For other classes, MDR Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires sufficient access to the other manufacturer's data. It does not require a contract under Article 61(5). The same over-broad attribution to Article 61(5) appears at lines 163 and 184.
correct: Article 61(5): contract required for implantable and Class III devices claiming equivalence to another manufacturer's device. For all classes, Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires sufficient access to the equivalent device's data.
correctedText: Under EU MDR Article 61(5), manufacturers of implantable and Class III devices demonstrating equivalence to a device of another manufacturer must have a contract in place (for other device classes, Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires the manufacturer to demonstrate sufficient levels of access to the data on the equivalent device)

quote: An equivalent device must have the same clinical purpose, similar design, and use similar materials.
error: The biological criterion is wrong. MDR Annex XIV Part A Section 3 and MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 A1 require the SAME materials or substances in contact with the same human tissues or body fluids, not similar materials.
correct: Biologically, the device must use the same materials or substances in contact with the same human tissues or body fluids, for a similar kind and duration of contact.
correctedText: An equivalent device must have the same clinical purpose, similar design, and use the same materials or substances in contact with the same human tissues or body fluids, for a similar kind and duration of contact.

quote: EU MDR Article 61(5) requires access to the equivalent device's technical documentation via contract when claiming equivalence to another manufacturer's device
error: The Article 61(5) contract requirement is limited to implantable and Class III devices. For other classes, Annex XIV Part A requires sufficient access to the data, not a contract.
correct: For implantable and Class III devices, Article 61(5) requires a contract giving full, ongoing access. For other classes, Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires sufficient levels of access to the data.
correctedText: For implantable and Class III devices, EU MDR Article 61(5) requires a contract allowing full, ongoing access to the equivalent device's technical documentation when claiming equivalence to another manufacturer's device; for other device classes, MDR Annex XIV Part A requires sufficient access to the equivalent device's data to justify the equivalence claim

quote: Same clinical condition, same clinical purpose, same clinical effect, same site in body, same target population
error: Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires a SIMILAR population (including age, anatomy and physiology), not the same population. It also requires the same kind of user and similar relevant critical performance, not the 'same clinical effect'.
correct: Same clinical condition or purpose (similar severity and stage of disease), same site in the body, similar population, same kind of user, and similar relevant critical performance for the expected clinical effect.
correctedText: Same clinical condition or purpose (including similar severity and stage of disease), same site in the body, similar population (age, anatomy, physiology), same kind of user, similar relevant critical performance for the expected clinical effect

quote: This data feeds into the CER as clinical experience per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7.
error: Section 7 covers scope (Stage 0). Post-market and clinical-experience data held by the manufacturer is identified under Section 8 (Stage 1, Section 8.1).
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8.1.
correctedText: This data feeds into the CER as clinical experience per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8.1.

quote: The CER must include a complete description of the device per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section A1.
error: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A1 is 'Demonstration of equivalence'; these same flow files cite it correctly for that elsewhere. The typical contents of a device description are in Appendix A3.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3 (Device description – typical contents).
correctedText: The CER must include a complete description of the device per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3 (device description – typical contents).

quote: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section A1.
error: Appendix A1 covers demonstrating equivalence, not the device description.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3.
correctedText: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3.

quote: all variants/models covered by this CER. Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section A1.
error: Appendix A1 covers demonstration of equivalence, not the device description.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3.
correctedText: all variants/models covered by this CER. Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3.

quote: Implantable as defined by EU MDR Article 2(5) — intended to be totally or partially introduced into the human body
error: This misstates the Article 2(5) definition. Being 'totally or partially introduced' alone describes any invasive device. Under Article 2(5), an implantable device must be introduced by surgical intervention and intended to remain in place after the procedure. A partially introduced device must be intended to remain for at least 30 days.
correct: Article 2(5): a device intended to be totally introduced into the body, or to replace an epithelial surface or the surface of the eye, by surgical intervention, and to remain after the procedure. A device partially introduced by surgical intervention counts only if it is intended to remain for at least 30 days.
correctedText: Implantable as defined by EU MDR Article 2(5) — intended to be totally introduced into the human body (or to replace an epithelial surface or the surface of the eye) by clinical intervention and to remain in place after the procedure; a device partially introduced by clinical intervention qualifies if intended to remain in place for at least 30 days

quote: BSI 0086, TUV SUD 0123
error: 0086 is BSI's UK body, now a UK Approved Body under UKCA. It is not an EU MDR Notified Body and cannot certify CE marking under the MDR. BSI's EU MDR Notified Body is BSI Group The Netherlands, number 2797.
correct: e.g. BSI Group The Netherlands 2797, TÜV SÜD 0123.
correctedText: BSI Group The Netherlands 2797, TÜV SÜD 0123

quote: Name and NB number of the Notified Body (e.g. BSI 0086, TUV SUD 0123)
error: Since Brexit, BSI 0086 is a UK Approved Body and is not designated as an EU MDR Notified Body. BSI's EU MDR Notified Body is BSI Group The Netherlands B.V., number 2797.
correct: Give an EU-designated Notified Body as the example, e.g. BSI 2797 or TÜV SÜD 0123.
correctedText: Name and NB number of the Notified Body (e.g. BSI 2797, TUV SUD 0123)

quote: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section A1, the scope of the clinical evaluation is directly defined by the intended purpose.
error: Appendix A1 covers equivalence. The scope of the clinical evaluation (Stage 0) is MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7 (Definition of the scope of the clinical evaluation).
correctedText: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7 (definition of the scope of the clinical evaluation), the scope of the clinical evaluation is directly defined by the intended purpose.

quote: Per EU MDR Article 2(12), the intended purpose includes the medical condition, target patient population, and clinical benefits.
error: Article 2(12) defines intended purpose as the use for which a device is intended according to the manufacturer's label, IFU, promotional or sales materials and clinical evaluation. It does not list medical condition, patient population or clinical benefits. Those elements are required in the device description under Annex II Section 1.1.
correct: Article 2(12) defines intended purpose by the manufacturer's data. Indications, patient population and related elements are required by MDR Annex II Section 1.1.
correctedText: Per EU MDR Article 2(12), the intended purpose is the use for which the device is intended according to the manufacturer's label, IFU, promotional or sales materials and clinical evaluation; MDR Annex II Section 1.1 requires the device description to state the intended purpose together with the intended patient population, medical conditions and indications, and the clinical evaluation plan (Annex XIV Part A) must specify the intended clinical benefits.

quote: the strictest classification prevails per Article 51(7)
error: Article 51 has no paragraph 7. The rule that the strictest applicable rule decides the class is in MDR Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5.
correct: EU MDR Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5.
correctedText: the strictest rule resulting in the higher classification applies per Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5

quote: For devices where multiple rules apply, the strictest classification prevails per Article 51(7).
error: The 'strictest rule applies' principle is an implementing rule in Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5. Article 51 does not contain it.
correct: Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5: where several rules apply, the strictest rule, giving the higher class, applies.
correctedText: For devices where multiple rules apply, the strictest rule resulting in the higher classification applies per Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5.

quote: GSPR 1 (safety/performance), 2 (risk management), 6 (clinical benefits), 8 (performance characteristics)
error: The wrong GSPR numbers are given as the ones usually needing clinical evidence. GSPR 6 is about lifetime performance, not clinical benefits. GSPR 8 is about side-effects and residual risks weighed against benefits, not performance characteristics. Risk management is GSPR 3, not GSPR 2.
correct: GSPR 1 (performance and safety), GSPR 8 (side-effects acceptable against benefits) and, where relevant, GSPRs 2-4 (risk reduction, risk management system, residual risk) and 6 (lifetime performance) are the ones usually supported by clinical data.
correctedText: GSPR 1 (performance and safety, acceptable benefit-risk), 8 (side-effects acceptable against benefits) and, where relevant, 2-4 (risk reduction, risk management, residual risk) and 6 (performance over the device lifetime)

quote: Typically includes GSPR 1 (safety/performance), 2 (risk management), 6 (clinical benefits), 8 (performance characteristics).
error: The GSPR numbers are given the wrong subjects. GSPR 2 is risk reduction as far as possible (risk management is GSPR 3). GSPR 6 is keeping performance over the device lifetime, not clinical benefits. GSPR 8 is minimising undesirable side-effects, not performance characteristics.
correct: The GSPRs that usually need clinical evidence are GSPR 1 (performance and safety, benefit-risk), GSPR 8 (undesirable side-effects acceptable against benefits) and, where relevant, GSPR 6 (lifetime). GSPR 2 is risk reduction as far as possible and GSPR 3 is risk management.
correctedText: Typically includes GSPR 1 (performance, safety and acceptable benefit-risk), 8 (undesirable side-effects minimised and acceptable against the benefits) and, where relevant, 6 (performance and safety over the device lifetime); GSPRs 2-3 (risk reduction and risk management) are usually supported by clinical data as an input.

quote: clinical benefits (6), chemical properties (7), performance characteristics (8), design for safety (9)
error: Most of this description of MDR Annex I Chapter I is wrong. Risk management is GSPR 3, not GSPR 2. GSPR 6 covers performance over the device lifetime under normal conditions of use, not clinical benefits. GSPR 7 covers transport and storage, not chemical properties. GSPR 8 says known risks and side-effects are minimised and acceptable against benefits; it is not about performance characteristics. GSPR 9 covers Annex XVI products with no medical purpose, not design for safety.
correct: MDR Annex I Chapter I: 1 performance and safety; 2 reduce risks as far as possible; 3 risk management system; 4 risk control measures and information on residual risk; 5 use error and ergonomics; 6 performance and safety over the device lifetime; 7 transport and storage; 8 known risks and side-effects minimised and acceptable against benefits; 9 Annex XVI products.
correctedText: performance and safety over the device lifetime (6), transport and storage (7), known risks and side-effects minimised and acceptable against benefits (8), Annex XVI products without a medical purpose (9)

quote: risk management (2), acceptability of benefit-risk (3-4), design for performance (5), clinical benefits (6), chemical properties (7), performance characteristics (8), design for safety (9)
error: This mapping of the Chapter I GSPRs is wrong. In MDR Annex I: GSPR 2 is reducing risk as far as possible; 3 is the risk management system; 4 is risk control measures; 5 is use error and ergonomics; 6 is that performance is kept over the device lifetime; 7 is transport and storage; 8 is that undesirable side-effects are minimised and acceptable; 9 is Annex XVI products. None of them is 'clinical benefits' or 'chemical properties'.
correct: 1 performance and safety; 2 risk reduction as far as possible; 3 risk management system; 4 risk control measures and information for safety; 5 use error and ergonomics; 6 characteristics kept during lifetime; 7 transport and storage; 8 side-effects minimised and acceptable against benefits; 9 Annex XVI products without a medical purpose.
correctedText: risk reduction as far as possible (2), risk management system (3), risk control measures and information for safety (4), use error and ergonomics (5), performance maintained over device lifetime (6), transport and storage (7), side-effects minimised and acceptable against benefits (8), Annex XVI products without a medical purpose (9)

quote: chemical/physical/biological properties (10-11), infection (12), substances (13-14), software (15-17), active devices (18-22)
error: This misnumbers MDR Annex I Chapter II. Infection and microbial contamination is GSPR 11, not 12. GSPR 12 covers devices that incorporate a medicinal substance or are made of substances absorbed by the body. GSPR 13 covers materials of biological origin. GSPR 14 covers construction and interaction with the environment. GSPRs 15 and 16 cover diagnostic or measuring function and radiation, not software. Software is GSPR 17. GSPRs 20-22 (mechanical and thermal risks, energy or substance supply, lay-person devices) are not limited to active devices.
correct: 10 chemical, physical and biological properties; 11 infection and microbial contamination; 12 medicinal substances and absorbed substances; 13 materials of biological origin; 14 construction and interaction with the environment; 15 diagnostic and measuring function; 16 radiation; 17 electronic programmable systems and software; 18 active devices; 19 active implantable devices; 20 mechanical and thermal risks; 21 supply of energy or substances; 22 lay-person devices.
correctedText: chemical/physical/biological properties (10), infection and microbial contamination (11), medicinal and absorbed substances (12), materials of biological origin (13), construction and environment (14), diagnostic/measuring function (15), radiation (16), electronic programmable systems and software (17), active and active implantable devices (18-19), mechanical/thermal and energy/substance supply risks (20-21), lay-person devices (22)

quote: Includes: chemical/physical/biological properties (10-11), infection (12), substances (13-14), software (15-17), active devices (18-22)
error: This mapping of the Chapter II GSPRs is wrong. GSPR 11 is infection and microbial contamination. GSPR 12 is devices incorporating a medicinal substance or made of absorbed substances. GSPR 13 is materials of biological origin. GSPR 14 is construction and interaction with the environment. GSPR 15 is diagnostic and measuring function. GSPR 16 is radiation. Software is GSPR 17 only. GSPRs 18-19 are active and active implantable devices. GSPRs 20-22 are mechanical and thermal risks, devices supplying energy or substances, and lay-person devices.
correct: 10 chemical/physical/biological properties; 11 infection and microbial contamination; 12 medicinal substances and absorbed substances; 13 biological origin; 14 construction and environment; 15 diagnostic and measuring function; 16 radiation; 17 software and electronic programmable systems; 18 active devices; 19 active implantable devices; 20 mechanical and thermal risks; 21 energy or substance delivery; 22 lay persons.
correctedText: Includes: chemical/physical/biological properties (10), infection and microbial contamination (11), medicinal and absorbed substances (12), materials of biological origin (13), construction and environment (14), diagnostic/measuring function (15), radiation (16), software and electronic programmable systems (17), active and active implantable devices (18-19), mechanical/thermal risks (20), energy or substance delivery (21), lay-person devices (22)

quote: Labeling requirements including label, IFU, implant card per Annex I Section 23
error: The implant card is not an Annex I Section 23 requirement. Section 23 covers the label and the instructions for use. The implant card and the information supplied to implanted patients are set out in MDR Article 18.
correct: Label and IFU: MDR Annex I Section 23. Implant card: MDR Article 18.
correctedText: Labeling requirements including label and IFU per Annex I Section 23 (implant card per MDR Article 18)

quote: provide justification that the alternative approach provides equivalent safety and performance per EU MDR Article 9(2)
error: The wrong paragraph is cited. Article 9(2) is the presumption of conformity for devices that conform to the CS. The duty to comply with CS unless an equivalent alternative is justified is in Article 9(3).
correct: EU MDR Article 9(3).
correctedText: provide justification that the alternative approach provides equivalent safety and performance per EU MDR Article 9(3)

quote: provides equivalent safety and performance per EU MDR Article 9(2)
error: Article 9(2) is the presumption of conformity for devices that meet a Common Specification. The rule that manufacturers must comply with a CS unless they justify an at-least-equivalent alternative is in Article 9(3).
correct: EU MDR Article 9(3).
correctedText: provides equivalent safety and performance per EU MDR Article 9(3)

quote: ISO 14155:2020 Annex A provides guidance on literature search methodology for clinical investigations.
error: ISO 14155:2020 Annex A is the Clinical investigation plan (CIP). ISO 14155 has no annex on literature search methodology. The literature search and review protocol for a CER is in MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A5.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A5 (literature search and literature review protocol). ISO 14155:2020 Annex A is the CIP.
correctedText: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A5 sets out the key elements of the literature search and literature review protocol.

quote: Per ICH Q1A(R2)–Q1F, stability studies must be conducted
error: ICH Q1F (Stability Data Package for Registration Applications in Climatic Zones III and IV) was withdrawn by ICH in 2006. It is not a guideline in force and should not be cited as part of the current stability guidance set. The file header comment repeats the citation, but that comment is not shown to clients.
correct: Cite ICH Q1A(R2) through Q1E (Q1A(R2), Q1B, Q1C, Q1D, Q1E). For Zone III/IV conditions, refer to WHO stability guidance (TRS 1010 Annex 10). Q1F was withdrawn in 2006.
correctedText: Per ICH Q1A(R2)–Q1E, stability studies must be conducted

quote: 30°C / 65% RH (Long-Term, Zone III/IV)
error: 30°C/65% RH as the long-term condition for Zones III and IV came from ICH Q1F, which was withdrawn in 2006. Under current WHO zone definitions, 30°C/65% RH is Zone IVa only. Zone III is 30°C/35% RH and Zone IVb is 30°C/75% RH. The same label appears at line 164 for the drug product.
correct: 30°C/65% RH is the long-term condition for Zone IVa, and an ICH Q1A(R2) alternative long-term condition. Zone IVb is 30°C/75% RH and Zone III is 30°C/35% RH.
correctedText: 30°C / 65% RH (Long-Term, Zone IVa)

quote: 'Per ICH Q6A (Section 3) and Q6B (Section 3), characterize relevant physicochemical properties
error: ICH Q6B Section 3 is 'Justification of the Specification', not the characterization of physicochemical or higher-order structure properties.
correct: Physicochemical properties of biotech products are in ICH Q6B Section 2.1.1 ('Physicochemical properties'), under 2.1 Characterisation.
correctedText: 'Per ICH Q6A (Section 3) and Q6B (Section 2.1, Characterisation), characterize relevant physicochemical properties

quote: reference: 'ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management, ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.6',
error: ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.6 does not cover risk assessment. In Part I, Section 2.6 is 'Compatibility'. In Part II (the Annex), Section 2.6 is 'Product Lifecycle Management and Continual Improvement'.
correct: The section on risk assessment for identifying CPPs and CQAs is ICH Q8(R2) Part II Section 2.3, 'Risk Assessment: Linking Material Attributes and Process Parameters to Drug Product CQAs'.
correctedText: reference: 'ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management, ICH Q8(R2) Part II Section 2.3',

quote: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management, ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.6
error: Section 2.6 of ICH Q8(R2) Part I is 'Compatibility'. In the Annex (Part II), Section 2.6 is product lifecycle management. Neither covers quality risk assessment for identifying CPPs and CQAs. That topic is Q8(R2) Part II Section 2.3, 'Risk Assessment: Linking Material Attributes and Process Parameters to Drug Product CQAs'.
correct: ICH Q9, ICH Q8(R2) Part II (Annex) Section 2.3 (Risk Assessment)
correctedText: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management, ICH Q8(R2) Part II (Annex) Section 2.3 (Risk Assessment)

quote: Per ICH Q11, starting materials should be commercially available substances with well-defined specifications.
error: ICH Q11 does not require starting materials to be commercially available. Its Section 5 criteria are that the material has defined chemical properties and structure, is not a non-isolated intermediate, is incorporated as a significant structural fragment, and sits enough steps upstream. Commercial availability is only one case discussed in the Q11 Q&A, for justifying a commercially available chemical as a starting material. It is not a general requirement.
correct: Per ICH Q11 Section 5, a starting material should be a substance with defined chemical properties and structure, controlled by an appropriate specification, and incorporated as a significant structural fragment. Commercial availability is not required.
correctedText: Per ICH Q11, starting materials should be substances with defined chemical properties and structure, controlled by appropriate specifications, and incorporated as significant structural fragments of the drug substance; commercial availability is not itself a requirement.

quote: reference: 'ICH Q11, FDA Guidance on Drug Shortages (2023)',
error: I know of no FDA guidance titled 'Drug Shortages' issued in 2023. The citation looks invented.
correct: Cite a real FDA guidance. 'Risk Management Plans to Mitigate the Potential for Drug Shortages' was a draft in May 2022. 'Notifying FDA of a Permanent Discontinuance or Interruption in Manufacturing Under Section 506C of the FD&C Act' covers shortage notification.
correctedText: reference: 'ICH Q11; FDA draft guidance, Risk Management Plans to Mitigate the Potential for Drug Shortages',

quote: 'Per ICH Q6A (Section 3.1) for small molecules and Q6B (Section 3) for biologics, provide evidence confirming the molecular structure.
error: ICH Q6A Section 3.1 is 'Specifications: Definition and Justification', and ICH Q6B Section 3 is 'Justification of the Specification'. Neither section covers structural characterization.
correct: Characterization of biotech products is in ICH Q6B Section 2.1 ('Characterisation', which includes physicochemical properties and structure). Structure elucidation evidence goes in CTD 3.2.S.3.1 (ICH M4Q). Q6A does not have a structural-characterization section.
correctedText: 'Per ICH M4Q (CTD Section 3.2.S.3.1, Elucidation of Structure and other Characteristics), and for biologics ICH Q6B (Section 2.1, Characterisation), provide evidence confirming the molecular structure.

quote: Identification threshold ≥ 0.10% or ≥ 0.05%. Qualification threshold ≥ 0.15% or ≥ 0.05%.
error: For a maximum daily dose of 2 g/day or less, ICH Q3A(R2) Attachment 1 sets the identification threshold at 0.10% or 1.0 mg per day total daily intake, whichever is lower, and the qualification threshold at 0.15% or 1.0 mg per day TDI, whichever is lower. The text leaves out the 1.0 mg/day alternative. For doses above about 0.67 g/day (qualification) or 1 g/day (identification), that alternative is the threshold that applies, so the percentages given are wrong for those doses.
correct: Q3A(R2), dose ≤2 g/day: reporting 0.05%; identification 0.10% or 1.0 mg/day TDI, whichever is lower; qualification 0.15% or 1.0 mg/day TDI, whichever is lower. Dose >2 g/day: reporting 0.03%, identification 0.05%, qualification 0.05%.
correctedText: Identification threshold: 0.10% or 1.0 mg/day total daily intake, whichever is lower (dose ≤ 2g/day), or 0.05% (dose > 2g/day). Qualification threshold: 0.15% or 1.0 mg/day total daily intake, whichever is lower (dose ≤ 2g/day), or 0.05% (dose > 2g/day).

quote: Confirmed mutagenic impurities (Class 1, 2, or 3)
error: In ICH M7, Class 3 means an alerting structure, unrelated to the drug substance structure, with no mutagenicity data. A Class 3 impurity is not a confirmed mutagen. Only Class 1 (known mutagenic carcinogens) and Class 2 (known mutagens with unknown carcinogenic potential) are confirmed mutagenic.
correct: Confirmed mutagenic impurities are ICH M7 Class 1 or 2. Class 3 impurities have alerts but no data, and are treated as mutagenic until tested, for example by an Ames test.
correctedText: Mutagenic impurities requiring control (confirmed Class 1 or 2, or alerting Class 3)

quote: Commercial processes must be validated before NDA/BLA approval.
error: FDA's 2011 Process Validation guidance ties successful PPQ to commercial distribution, not to application approval: a manufacturer must complete PPQ before any batch is commercially distributed. For NDAs there is no rule that PPQ is finished before approval. The same claim appears at line 1172 ('FDA expects PPQ to be complete before NDA/BLA approval') and line 1182. Line 1182 also contradicts itself, since it goes on to describe a commitment to complete PPQ before commercial distribution.
correct: Per FDA's Process Validation guidance (2011), PPQ must be completed successfully before commercial distribution of product. For BLAs, FDA typically expects PPQ or validation data in the application. For NDAs, PPQ can be completed after approval, as long as it is done before commercial distribution.
correctedText: Under that guidance, PPQ must be completed successfully before the product is commercially distributed; for BLAs, process validation data are generally expected in the application.

quote: Per ICH E9 Section 5.5, the primary analysis should be fully pre-specified in the statistical analysis plan (SAP).
error: ICH E9 Section 5.5 is 'Estimation, Confidence Intervals and Hypothesis Testing'. Pre-specifying the analysis in the SAP is covered in Section 5.1, 'Prespecification of the Analysis'.
correct: Per ICH E9 Section 5.1 (Prespecification of the Analysis), the primary analysis should be pre-specified in the protocol/statistical analysis plan.
correctedText: Per ICH E9 Section 5.1 (Prespecification of the Analysis), the primary analysis should be fully pre-specified in the protocol and statistical analysis plan (SAP).

quote: Per FDA Guidance "Safety Reporting Requirements for INDs and BA/BE Studies" (2012), AESIs should be defined in the protocol and monitored via Standardized MedDRA Queries (SMQs) or Customized MedDRA Queries (CMQs).
error: This is a misattribution. The 2012 FDA final guidance on IND/BA-BE safety reporting covers 21 CFR 312.32/320.31 expedited reporting: definitions, causality, the 15-day and 7-day clocks, and aggregate analysis. It does not require AESIs to be defined in the protocol, and it does not tell sponsors to monitor them with SMQs or CMQs.
correct: Defining AESIs in the protocol and searching for them with SMQs or CMQs is industry practice that draws on CIOMS VI and MedDRA guidance. The 2012 FDA safety reporting guidance does not require it.
correctedText: In line with CIOMS VI and common industry practice (not a requirement of FDA's 2012 guidance "Safety Reporting Requirements for INDs and BA/BE Studies", which addresses expedited reporting under 21 CFR 312.32), AESIs should be defined in the protocol and monitored via Standardized MedDRA Queries (SMQs) or Customized MedDRA Queries (CMQs).

quote: while the PP population is preferred for non-inferiority and equivalence trials
error: ICH E9 (Section 5.2.3) does not say the per-protocol set is preferred for equivalence or non-inferiority trials. It says only that using the full analysis set in those trials is generally not conservative, and that its role should be considered carefully. Both analyses are expected, and conclusions should be robust across them (FDA's 2016 non-inferiority guidance says the same).
correct: Per ICH E9 Section 5.2.3, the full analysis set is generally primary for superiority trials. In equivalence and non-inferiority trials, the full analysis set is not conservative, so both the FAS and the PP analyses should be presented and the conclusions should hold under both.
correctedText: while in non-inferiority and equivalence trials the full analysis set is generally not conservative, so both the ITT and PP analyses should be presented and the conclusions should be consistent across them

quote: the routes are a De Novo request or a 510(k) for the new intended use.
error: A 510(k) cannot clear a new intended use. A device with a different intended use from its predicate is not substantially equivalent by definition (21 CFR 807.100(b); FD&C Act 513(i)). This text tells clients a 510(k) is a valid route for a new intended use, which contradicts the flow's own warning at line 424.
correct: If the indications and the technology come from different devices, the options are: a 510(k) on a single predicate (or several predicates, each with the same intended use) that has both the intended use and comparable technology, or a De Novo request (or a PMA) where no such predicate exists. A new intended use cannot be reached through a 510(k).
correctedText: the routes are a 510(k) against a predicate (or predicates, each with the same intended use) that has both the intended use and comparable technological characteristics, or a De Novo request where no such predicate exists; a new intended use cannot be cleared through a 510(k).

quote: reference: 'FD&C Act 513(f)(2)(A); 21 CFR 860.220(a)',
error: The finding cites 21 CFR 860.220(a) for the two conditions that make a device eligible for a De Novo request: a prior NSE determination, or no legally marketed predicate. 860.220 sets out what a De Novo request must contain; paragraph (a) covers administrative information. The eligibility conditions are in 21 CFR 860.200, 'Purpose and applicability', in Subpart D.
correct: FD&C Act 513(f)(2)(A); 21 CFR 860.200 (who may submit a De Novo request: after an NSE determination, or when there is no legally marketed predicate).
correctedText: reference: 'FD&C Act 513(f)(2)(A); 21 CFR 860.200',

quote: Devices with patient contact >24 hours require a comprehensive biocompatibility evaluation including systemic toxicity, genotoxicity, and (for implants) implantation and chronic toxicity testing per ISO 10993-1 Table A.1.
error: The statement says ISO 10993-1 Table A.1 requires systemic toxicity and genotoxicity for every device with more than 24 hours of contact. That is wrong. For surface devices on intact skin, Table A.1 lists only cytotoxicity, sensitization and irritation at every duration, including prolonged and permanent. Chronic toxicity is an endpoint only for long-term (permanent, more than 30 days) contact, so it is not called for in every implant with more than 24 hours of contact. The check fires as 'critical' on any prolonged or permanent contact, including intact-skin devices.
correct: ISO 10993-1:2018 Table A.1 sets the endpoints by both contact category and duration. Systemic toxicity and genotoxicity apply only to some categories with prolonged or permanent contact (for example breached surfaces, externally communicating devices and implants), not to intact-skin surface devices. Chronic toxicity applies to long-term contact.
correctedText: Devices with patient contact >24 hours need a biocompatibility evaluation of the endpoints that ISO 10993-1 Table A.1 assigns to their contact category and duration. Depending on the category, these can include systemic toxicity and genotoxicity (for example, for breached-surface, externally communicating and implant devices), implantation, and, for long-term (>30 days) contact, chronic toxicity. Surface devices on intact skin require only cytotoxicity, sensitization and irritation.

quote: FDA conducts a pre-approval inspection for most PMA applications per 21 CFR 814.20(b)(4)
error: 21 CFR 814.20(b)(4) sets out what the PMA application must contain: a complete description of the device, its components, properties and principles of operation, and the methods, facilities and controls used to manufacture it. It says nothing about FDA conducting a pre-approval inspection, so it is the wrong citation for that statement.
correct: Pre-approval inspection is FDA's practice in the PMA review under 21 CFR 814.44 (approval may depend on a finding that the manufacturing facilities, methods and controls comply with 21 CFR Part 820). Under 21 CFR 814.45(a)(3), FDA may deny approval if the facilities, methods or controls do not conform to Part 820. 814.20(b)(4) is only the application-content requirement for the manufacturing description.
correctedText: FDA conducts a pre-approval inspection for most PMA applications; approval may be denied if the manufacturing methods, facilities or controls do not conform to 21 CFR Part 820 (21 CFR 814.45(a)(3))

quote: The biological evaluation plan and report should follow the structure in ISO 10993-1 Annex A.
error: In ISO 10993-1:2018, which this flow cites as its edition at lines 795 and 804, Annex A is the table of biological endpoints to address (Table A.1). It does not set a structure for the biological evaluation plan or report. Guidance on carrying out the biological evaluation within the risk management process is in Annex B.
correct: ISO 10993-1:2018 Annex A (Table A.1) lists the biological endpoints to consider for each contact category and duration. Annex B gives guidance on conducting the biological evaluation within a risk management process, including planning and reporting.
correctedText: The biological evaluation plan and report should address the endpoints identified in ISO 10993-1 Annex A (Table A.1), with the evaluation conducted within a risk management process as described in ISO 10993-1 Annex B.

quote: MRI labeling per ASTM F2503 is required for implantable devices
error: No regulation requires MRI labeling per ASTM F2503 for implantable devices. ASTM F2503 is an FDA-recognized consensus standard. FDA's guidance 'Testing and Labeling Medical Devices for Safety in the Magnetic Resonance (MR) Environment' (2023) recommends MR safety labeling for implants that may enter the MR environment. A recommendation is not a requirement.
correct: FDA recommends, through guidance, MR safety testing and labeling (MR Safe, MR Conditional or MR Unsafe, using the ASTM F2503 terms) for implants that may enter the MR environment. ASTM F2503 is a recognized standard, not a regulatory requirement.
correctedText: FDA guidance recommends MR safety testing and labeling (MR Safe, MR Conditional or MR Unsafe, using the terms in the FDA-recognized standard ASTM F2503) for implantable devices that may enter the MR environment

quote: Dun & Bradstreet number required for FDA submissions per OMB guidance.
error: Form FDA 1571 and 21 CFR 312.23 do not require a DUNS number for an IND. The OMB DUNS requirement applied to federal grants and awards, and the federal government replaced DUNS with the SAM Unique Entity ID in April 2022. FDA uses DUNS for establishment registration and listing, not IND submission.
correct: An IND does not require a DUNS number. DUNS or FEI numbers apply to establishment registration and listing and to some application forms, not to Form FDA 1571.
correctedText: Optional. An IND (Form FDA 1571) does not require a DUNS number; FDA uses DUNS mainly to identify establishments for drug establishment registration and listing.

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7), the IND must include a description of the drug substance and drug product, including the name, chemical structure, mechanism of action, route of administration, and proposed indication.
error: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7) is the chemistry, manufacturing and controls section. Route of administration, pharmacological class and broad objectives belong to the introductory statement, 312.23(a)(3). Mechanism of action belongs to pharmacology, 312.23(a)(8)(i). Neither is an (a)(7) requirement.
correct: Name, structure, pharmacological class, formulation, route and objectives go in the introductory statement (21 CFR 312.23(a)(3)(i)). Mechanism of action goes under 312.23(a)(8)(i). Drug substance and drug product CMC goes under 312.23(a)(7).
correctedText: Per 21 CFR 312.23, the IND must identify the drug: its name, structural formula, pharmacological class, formulation and route of administration go in the introductory statement (312.23(a)(3)), together with the broad objectives and proposed indication; mechanism of action goes in the pharmacology section (312.23(a)(8)); and the description of the drug substance and drug product goes in the chemistry, manufacturing and controls section (312.23(a)(7)).

quote: Not yet — typically required before Phase 3 / NDA
error: Under ICH M3(R2) Section 8, carcinogenicity studies, when needed, are normally completed for marketing approval. They are not needed before large-scale clinical trials (Phase 3) unless there is a special concern. 'Before Phase 3' is wrong.
correct: When needed, carcinogenicity studies are typically completed before the marketing application (NDA/BLA). Phase 3 can proceed without them unless there is a specific cause for concern.
correctedText: Not yet — typically required for the marketing application (NDA), not before Phase 3 unless there is a specific concern

quote: FDA Guidance "Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products" (2017)
error: The December 2017 draft was replaced by the September 2023 revised guidance of the same title, issued under PDUFA VII. That revision added Type D and INTERACT meetings. Citing the 2017 version as current refers to a superseded document.
correct: FDA Guidance "Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products" (September 2023 revision), which describes Type A, B, B (EOP), C, D and INTERACT meetings.
correctedText: FDA draft guidance "Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products" (revised September 2023, which replaced the 2017 draft and added Type D and INTERACT meetings)

quote: placeholder: 'e.g., Division of Oncology Products 1, Office of New Drugs / CDER',
error: CDER's 2019 reorganisation of the Office of New Drugs ended the 'Division of Oncology Products 1'. Oncology review now sits in the Office of Oncologic Diseases, in the Divisions of Oncology 1, 2 and 3 and the hematology divisions.
correct: e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, Office of New Drugs / CDER
correctedText: placeholder: 'e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, Office of New Drugs / CDER',

quote: e.g., Division of Oncology Products 1, Office of New Drugs / CDER
error: CDER reorganised the Office of New Drugs in 2019-2020, and 'Division of Oncology Products 1' no longer exists. Oncology review now sits in the Office of Oncologic Diseases, under Divisions of Oncology 1, 2 and 3 and the hematologic malignancies divisions.
correct: e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, Office of New Drugs / CDER.
correctedText: e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, Office of New Drugs / CDER

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.31 (Amendments to an IND), amendments must describe the nature and significance of each change.
error: 21 CFR 312.31 is titled "Information amendments". It does not cover IND amendments in general. Protocol amendments are a separate section, 312.30, and no CFR section is titled "Amendments to an IND".
correct: 21 CFR 312.31 (Information amendments). IND amendments as a whole fall under 21 CFR 312.30 (protocol amendments) and 312.31 (information amendments).
correctedText: Per 21 CFR 312.31 (Information amendments), an information amendment must state the nature and purpose of the amendment.

quote: Information amendments (21 CFR 312.31(b)) cover all other changes.
error: The scope rule (essential information not covered by a protocol amendment, an IND safety report or the annual report) is in 312.31(a), 'Requirement for information amendment'. 312.31(b) covers only the content and format of an information amendment.
correct: Information amendments (21 CFR 312.31(a)) cover essential information not within the scope of a protocol amendment, IND safety report or annual report.
correctedText: Information amendments (21 CFR 312.31(a)) cover essential information not within the scope of a protocol amendment, an IND safety report or the annual report.

quote: FDA agreement is binding unless the sponsor fails to follow the agreed-upon protocol.
error: The exceptions to an SPA agreement are incomplete. Under FD&C Act 505(b)(5)(C), FDA can also change the agreement with the sponsor's written agreement, or when a substantial scientific issue essential to judging safety or effectiveness is identified after testing has begun. Under the SPA guidance, it can also do so when the data the sponsor relied on prove false, misleading or materially incomplete.
correct: An SPA agreement binds the review division. It can change if the sponsor agrees in writing, if a substantial scientific issue essential to safety or effectiveness is identified after testing begins, if the sponsor does not follow the agreed protocol, or if the data it relied on prove false or incomplete.
correctedText: An SPA agreement binds FDA, but it can be changed with the sponsor's written agreement, or if a substantial scientific issue essential to determining safety or effectiveness is identified after testing begins (FD&C Act 505(b)(5)(C)); per FDA's SPA guidance it also no longer binds if the sponsor does not follow the agreed protocol or the data relied on prove false, misleading or materially incomplete.

quote: single-enantiomer development is generally preferred. A racemate requires justification.
error: FDA's 1992 Policy Statement for the Development of New Stereoisomeric Drugs states no preference for single enantiomers. It leaves the choice of racemate or single enantiomer to the sponsor and asks for stereochemistry-specific characterisation and controls either way.
correct: Under the 1992 FDA policy the sponsor may develop either a racemate or a single enantiomer. Either way, the stereoisomeric composition must be characterised and controlled, and the individual enantiomers' pharmacology and PK assessed.
correctedText: the sponsor may develop either a racemate or a single enantiomer; either way, the stereoisomeric composition must be characterised and controlled, and the individual enantiomers' pharmacology and pharmacokinetics assessed to support the choice.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) requires stability data at submission.
error: ICH Q1A(R2) sets the stability data package for registration (marketing) applications. It does not set IND stability requirements. IND stability content comes from 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(a)-(b) and FDA's IND CMC guidances (Phase 1 guidance of 1995; Phase 2/3 guidance of 2003): stability data adequate to cover the duration of the planned trial. The guidance at line 1411 makes the same misattribution: 'A minimum of 1-2 months accelerated data ... per ICH Q1A(R2)'.
correct: Under 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7) and FDA's IND CMC guidances, the IND must describe the stability program and give data showing the material stays within specification for the duration of the clinical study. ICH Q1A(R2) governs registration stability packages.
correctedText: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7) requires the IND to include stability information showing that the drug substance and drug product remain within specification for the planned clinical studies (ICH Q1A(R2) governs the registration stability package, not the IND).

quote: FDA requires all drug product sponsors to complete a nitrosamine impurity risk assessment per the current FDA guidance
error: The FDA nitrosamine guidance (Rev. 2, September 2024) is non-binding. Its recommendations are addressed to manufacturers and applicants of marketed products and of pending or approved NDAs, ANDAs and BLAs. It does not impose a requirement that IND sponsors complete the assessment before IND submission. The help text at line 1822 says the same: 'all sponsors must conduct a risk assessment'.
correct: FDA recommends (non-binding guidance) that manufacturers of APIs and drug products, chiefly for marketed products and marketing applications, assess and control nitrosamine risk. For an IND it is good practice to assess the risk early, but it is not a regulatory requirement for submission.
correctedText: FDA recommends (in non-binding guidance) that manufacturers and applicants assess and control nitrosamine impurity risk per the current FDA guidance

quote: a dedicated study is recommended when renal clearance accounts for ≥30% of total clearance or the drug has a narrow therapeutic index
error: FDA's renal impairment guidance has no 30% renal-clearance cut-off. It recommends characterising PK in renal impairment for most drugs intended for patients who may have impaired renal function, including drugs eliminated mainly by non-renal routes, because renal impairment also changes metabolism and transport. A reduced design is an option, not an exemption below 30%. The option 'Not needed — minimal renal elimination (<30%)' at line 1933 relies on the same false threshold.
correct: FDA recommends a renal impairment PK study for most drugs likely to be used in patients with renal impairment, whatever the main elimination route. A reduced or staged design is possible for drugs that are not mainly renally eliminated.
correctedText: a renal impairment PK study is recommended for most drugs likely to be used in patients with renal impairment, including drugs eliminated mainly by non-renal routes; a reduced or staged design may be acceptable when renal elimination is minor

quote: { value: 'planned', label: 'Planned — timing per ICH M3(R2) Table 3' }
error: ICH M3(R2) Table 3 lists the nonclinical studies recommended for exploratory clinical trials (Section 7, approaches 1–5). It says nothing about when reproductive or embryo-fetal development studies are due. That timing is set out in the text of Section 11.
correct: Timing per ICH M3(R2) Section 11 (Reproduction Toxicity Studies).
correctedText: { value: 'planned', label: 'Planned — timing per ICH M3(R2) Section 11 (Reproduction Toxicity Studies)' }

quote: Planned — timing per ICH M3(R2) Table 3
error: ICH M3(R2) Table 3 covers recommended nonclinical studies for exploratory clinical trials. Reproductive toxicity timing relative to enrolling WOCBP is set out in M3(R2) Section 11, not in a table. The finding at line 2000 makes the same miscitation: 'EFD studies to be completed per ICH M3(R2) Table 3'.
correct: Reproductive and developmental toxicity timing is given in ICH M3(R2) Section 11 (Reproduction toxicity studies, 11.3 Women of childbearing potential).
correctedText: Planned — timing per ICH M3(R2) Section 11

quote: requires embryo-fetal development (EFD) studies to be completed per ICH M3(R2) Table 3
error: ICH M3(R2) Table 3 covers the nonclinical studies recommended for exploratory clinical trials. The rules on when EFD studies are needed before enrolling WOCBP are in Section 11 (11.3), not in a table.
correct: EFD studies completed per ICH M3(R2) Section 11 (Reproduction Toxicity Studies).
correctedText: requires embryo-fetal development (EFD) studies to be completed per ICH M3(R2) Section 11 (Reproduction Toxicity Studies)

quote: All prescription drug and biologic labeling must follow the Physician Labeling Rule (PLR) format
error: PLR format is required only for applications submitted on or after June 30, 2006, and for those approved from June 30, 2001 onward, on the phased schedule. Older prescription products may keep the non-PLR format under 21 CFR 201.80 unless they convert.
correct: PLR format (21 CFR 201.56(d), 201.57) is required for new NDAs/BLAs/efficacy supplements submitted on or after June 30, 2006, and for products approved since June 30, 2001 on the implementation schedule. Older labeling may follow 21 CFR 201.80.
correctedText: Prescription drug and biologic labeling for new NDAs, BLAs and efficacy supplements, and for products approved since June 30, 2001 under the implementation schedule, must follow the Physician Labeling Rule (PLR) format; older products not yet converted may use the format in 21 CFR 201.80

quote: Electronic SPL submission to FDA DailyMed is required.
error: SPL is submitted to FDA, through the Electronic Submissions Gateway as part of the application or listing. DailyMed is the National Library of Medicine's public site, which shows SPL that FDA has received. Sponsors do not submit to DailyMed. Line 204 says the same wrong thing ('submitted ... to the FDA's DailyMed system').
correct: Content of labeling is submitted to FDA in SPL format (21 CFR 314.50(l)(1)(i); 601.14). NLM's DailyMed then publishes it.
correctedText: Electronic SPL submission to FDA is required (via the Electronic Submissions Gateway); FDA-received SPL is then published on the National Library of Medicine's DailyMed.

quote: list sections with substantive labeling changes within the past year
error: 21 CFR 201.57(a)(5) allows Recent Major Changes to list only five FPI sections: Boxed Warning, Indications and Usage, Dosage and Administration, Contraindications, and Warnings and Precautions. It does not cover any section with a substantive change.
correct: Recent Major Changes lists substantive changes approved or authorized within the past year, but only in the Boxed Warning, Indications and Usage, Dosage and Administration, Contraindications, or Warnings and Precautions sections, with the section number and the month/year of the change.
correctedText: list substantive labeling changes made within the past year to the Boxed Warning, Indications and Usage, Dosage and Administration, Contraindications, or Warnings and Precautions sections only

quote: Not all sections are required for every product — include only those relevant. Sections 9 (Drug Abuse and Dependence) and 16 (How Supplied / Storage and Handling) are commonly included.
error: Under 21 CFR 201.56(d), most FPI sections are mandatory. Only a few listed sections may be left out when they clearly do not apply, such as Boxed Warning, Drug Abuse and Dependence, Clinical Studies and References. Section 16 (How Supplied/Storage and Handling, 201.57(c)(17)) is required for every product, not just 'commonly included'. Contraindications (Section 4) must appear even when there are none, and then it says 'None'.
correct: FPI sections 1–8, 11–13, 16 and 17 are required. Section 4 must state 'None' if there are no contraindications. Only the sections that 201.56(d) allows to be left out when inapplicable (e.g., Boxed Warning, Section 9, 14, 15) may be dropped.
correctedText: Most FPI sections are required. Under 21 CFR 201.56(d), a section may be left out only when it is clearly inapplicable and is one of those the rule allows to be omitted, such as Boxed Warning, 9 (Drug Abuse and Dependence), 10 (Overdosage), 14 (Clinical Studies) and 15 (References). Section 16 (How Supplied / Storage and Handling) is required for every product. Section 4 (Contraindications) must appear, and it states "None" when there are none.

quote: FDA Guidance: REMS Integration with Labeling
error: FDA has never issued a guidance titled 'REMS Integration with Labeling'. The citation names a document that does not exist.
correct: Cite real REMS guidance, for example 'REMS: FDA's Application of Statutory Factors in Determining When a REMS Is Necessary' (2019) or 'Format and Content of a REMS Document' (2017), together with 21 CFR 201.57(c)(1) for the boxed warning.
correctedText: FD&C Act section 505-1 (REMS)

quote: FDA Guidance: Medication Guides — Distribution Requirements and Inclusion in REMS (2011)
error: This 2011 guidance covers when Medication Guides must be distributed and how they fit into REMS. It does not set or recommend a 6th-8th grade reading level, so it does not support the finding it is attached to.
correct: The readability requirement for Medication Guides is in 21 CFR 208.20(a) (nontechnical, understandable language). FDA's written consumer medication information guidance ('Useful Written Consumer Medication Information (CMI)', 2006) addresses readability.
correctedText: 21 CFR 208.20 — Medication Guide content and format (nontechnical, understandable language)

quote: Inactive ingredients, and Questions? phone number.

quote: 21 CFR 801.4; FDA Guidance: Medical Device Home-Use Initiative (2023)
error: No FDA guidance has this title, and there is none from 2023. The Medical Device Home Use Initiative was a 2010 CDRH initiative, not a guidance. quote: FDA Guidance: Medical Device Home-Use Initiative (2023)
error: No FDA guidance has this title or date. The Medical Device Home Use Initiative was launched in 2010. correct: FDA Guidance: Design Considerations for Devices Intended for Home Use (November 2014). Home-use labeling recommendations come from guidance, not from 21 CFR 801.4.
correctedText: FDA Guidance: Design Considerations for Devices Intended for Home Use (2014)

quote: Per 21 CFR 830, all medical devices must bear a Unique Device Identifier (UDI) on their label.

quote: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1), the NDA must contain a full description of the drug substance, its mechanism of action, dosage form, route, and all proposed strengths.
error: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1) is the chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) technical section. It requires a description of the drug substance's physical/chemical characteristics, manufacture and controls, but not the mechanism of action or the proposed brand name. Mechanism and pharmacologic class belong to the application summary (314.50(c)) and the labeling (201.57(c)(13)).
correct: 314.50(d)(1) requires the CMC description of the drug substance and drug product; mechanism of action is presented in the summary (314.50(c)) and in labeling section 12.1 (21 CFR 201.57(c)(13)).
correctedText: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1), the NDA must contain a full chemistry, manufacturing and controls description of the drug substance and the drug product, including its dosage form, route, and all proposed strengths; the mechanism of action and pharmacologic class are addressed in the application summary (21 CFR 314.50(c)) and in labeling.

quote: Standard battery: (1) bacterial reverse mutation (Ames test), (2) in vitro chromosomal aberration or micronucleus assay, (3) in vivo micronucleus or equivalent.
error: This presents S2(R1) Option 1 as the only standard battery. ICH S2(R1) also accepts Option 2 (Ames + in vivo genotoxicity assessment in two tissues), which has no in vitro mammalian test.

correctedText: Standard battery (either option is acceptable): Option 1 - (1) bacterial reverse mutation (Ames test), (2) in vitro mammalian cell test (chromosomal aberration, micronucleus or mouse lymphoma Tk assay), (3) in vivo genotoxicity test (e.g., micronucleus); or Option 2 - (1) Ames test plus (2) in vivo genotoxicity assessment with two endpoints/tissues (e.g., micronucleus and a second in vivo assay such as the comet assay).

quote: Per FDA Guidance and ICH E1/E7, sponsors should analyze PK and safety data by sex.
error: Neither guideline covers sex-based analysis. ICH E1 covers the extent of population exposure for long-term treatment of non-life-threatening conditions, and ICH E7 covers geriatric populations.
correct: Sex-based analysis is addressed by FDA guidance (e.g., 'Evaluation of Sex-Specific Data in Medical Device Clinical Studies' for devices; for drugs, the 1993 FDA gender guideline and 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(v)-(vi) requiring effectiveness and safety data by gender, age and race), not ICH E1/E7.
correctedText: Per FDA guidance on sex differences in drug evaluation and 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5), sponsors should analyze PK and safety data by sex.

quote: FDA may require a REMS (with Medication Guide as a minimum element) when a boxed warning is warranted
error: A Medication Guide is not a minimum element of a REMS. Under 21 USC 355-1(d) the only required minimum is a timetable for assessments; a Medication Guide, communication plan and ETASU are each optional elements (355-1(e),(f)). A boxed warning also does not by itself trigger a REMS.
correct: FDA may require a REMS under 21 USC 355-1, which may include a Medication Guide, a communication plan and/or ETASU; the statutory minimum is a timetable for assessments.
correctedText: FDA may require a REMS under 21 USC 355-1 (which may include a Medication Guide, a communication plan and/or ETASU) when the serious risk behind a boxed warning needs more than labeling to manage

quote: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) and ICH E2D "Post-Approval Safety Data Management," all deaths and serious adverse events must be thoroughly analyzed.
error: ICH E2D covers post-approval safety data, so it is not the basis for analysing deaths and SAEs in a pre-approval clinical program for an NDA. 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) is the safety-update provision, not a deaths/SAE analysis requirement. The pre-approval framework is ICH E2A, ICH E3 section 12.3 and the ISS under 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a).
correct: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a) (integrated summary of safety), ICH E3 section 12.3 and ICH E2A, deaths and SAEs must be analysed; ICH E2D applies post-approval.
correctedText: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a) (integrated summary of safety) and ICH E3 (deaths, other serious and significant adverse events), all deaths and serious adverse events must be thoroughly analyzed.

quote: reference: '21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b); ICH E2A; ICH E2D',
error: ICH E2D is a post-approval guideline and does not govern analysis of drug-related deaths in the NDA clinical program. 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) is the safety-update requirement.
correct: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a); ICH E2A; ICH E3 section 12.3
correctedText: reference: '21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a); ICH E2A; ICH E3 (section 12.3)',

quote: All sequence numbers must follow the FDA Comprehensive Table of Contents (CTOCh) and CDER/CBER numbering conventions.
error: The FDA Comprehensive Table of Contents Headings and Hierarchy defines the CTD/eCTD heading structure, not eCTD sequence numbering. Sequence numbering is set by the FDA eCTD technical specifications / eCTD Technical Conformance Guide.
correct: Document placement must follow the FDA Comprehensive Table of Contents Headings and Hierarchy; sequence numbering follows the FDA eCTD technical specifications and eCTD Technical Conformance Guide.
correctedText: Document placement must follow the FDA Comprehensive Table of Contents Headings and Hierarchy, and sequence numbers must follow the FDA eCTD technical specifications and the eCTD Technical Conformance Guide.

quote: Per 21 USC 355-1(g), REMS assessments must be submitted at 18 months, 3 years, and 7 years after initial REMS approval
error: The 18-month / 3-year / 7th-year assessment timetable is in section 505-1(d) (21 USC 355-1(d), 'Minimal strategy'). Section 505-1(g) covers assessment and modification of an approved strategy. The statute also says 'in the 7th year', not 'at 7 years'.
correct: Per 21 USC 355-1(d), a REMS must include a timetable for assessments by 18 months and 3 years after initial approval and in the 7th year after approval, unless FDA specifies otherwise.
correctedText: Per 21 USC 355-1(d), REMS assessments must be submitted by 18 months, by 3 years, and in the 7th year after initial REMS approval

quote: FDAAA Section 505(o)(3)
error: Section 505(o)(3) is a section of the FD&C Act (added by FDAAA section 901), not a section of FDAAA. The same guidance also calls PMRs 'PMEs' (line 1916).
correct: FD&C Act section 505(o)(3) (21 USC 355(o)(3)), added by FDAAA section 901.
correctedText: FD&C Act section 505(o)(3) (added by FDAAA)

quote: PMC 3: Renal impairment PK study (Child-Pugh classification).

correct: PMC 3: Renal impairment PK study (stratified by eGFR/creatinine clearance); Child-Pugh applies to a hepatic impairment study.

quote: ICH E8(R1) Section 4 recommends the title convey the intervention, condition, phase, and design.

correctedText: The ICH M11 structured protocol template recommends the title convey the intervention, condition, phase, and design.

quote: ICH E9 Section 3.3 requires each arm to be adequately powered if formal pairwise comparisons are planned.
error: ICH E9 Section 3.3 is 'Type of Comparison' (superiority, equivalence/non-inferiority, dose-response). It sets no requirement about powering each arm. Sample size is covered in Section 3.5.
correct: Sample size and power considerations are in ICH E9 Section 3.5 (Sample Size). Section 3.3 covers the type of comparison.
correctedText: ICH E9 Section 3.5 (Sample Size) expects the sample size to be justified for the planned primary comparisons, including any formal pairwise comparisons between arms.

quote: reference: 'ICH E9 Section 2.2.5 — Multiplicity'
error: ICH E9 Section 2.2.5 is 'Multiple Primary Variables'. It is not a general multiplicity section and it does not cover pairwise comparisons across multiple treatment arms. Adjusting for multiple comparisons, such as multiple arms, is covered in ICH E9 Section 5.6, 'Adjustment of Significance and Confidence Levels'.
correct: ICH E9 Section 5.6 (Adjustment of Significance and Confidence Levels) for multiple-arm and pairwise multiplicity; Section 2.2.5 covers multiple primary variables only.
correctedText: reference: 'ICH E9 Section 5.6 — Adjustment of Significance and Confidence Levels'

quote: Trials exceeding 5,000 subjects require robust safety monitoring infrastructure, centralized statistical monitoring, and potentially a larger DSMB per FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial DSMBs (2006).
error: The 2006 FDA DMC guidance sets no 5,000-subject threshold and does not require centralized statistical monitoring or a larger DMC for big trials. The requirement is attributed to a source that does not contain it.
correct: The 2006 FDA guidance (Establishment and Operation of Clinical Trial Data Monitoring Committees) discusses when a DMC is advisable: large, multicenter or long trials with mortality or major morbidity endpoints. It sets no enrollment-size threshold or associated requirements.
correctedText: Trials exceeding 5,000 subjects warrant robust safety monitoring infrastructure and an independent Data Monitoring Committee; FDA Guidance on Establishment and Operation of Clinical Trial Data Monitoring Committees (2006) identifies large, multicenter trials with mortality or major morbidity endpoints as those where a DMC is generally advisable, and centralized statistical monitoring may be considered under a risk-based monitoring approach (ICH E6(R3)).
